questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's foodgrain procurement and export policy. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Food Corporation of India is a statutory body set up under the Food Corporations Act, 1964.
Buffer stocking norms for foodgrains are prescribed quarterly by the Government of India.
Export of all varieties of non-basmati rice is canalised exclusively through the National Cooperative Exports Limited.
The Minimum Support Price for paddy is announced by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
questions.explanation: FCI is indeed a statutory body under the 1964 Act, and buffer norms are prescribed quarterly (1 April, 1 July, 1 October, 1 January) — both correct. Only specific categories of non-basmati rice exports under government-to-government arrangements have been canalised through NCEL, not 'all varieties'. CACP only recommends MSP; it is the Cabinet (CCEA) that approves and announces it, so statement 4 is false.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: No fresh curbs on broken rice exports as India banks on steady paddy procurement
questions.pyqLink: Tests FCI's statutory status and the CACP-recommends/Government-announces distinction on MSP, a recurring UPSC trap (cf. UPSC 2020 question on MSP mechanics).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about India's reservoir storage and hydropower. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Central Water Commission functions under the Ministry of Jal Shakti and monitors live storage levels in India's major reservoirs.
The northeast monsoon is a significant source of rainfall for the southern peninsula even after the southwest monsoon has withdrawn.
Hydropower generation is unaffected by reservoir storage levels since turbines draw water from perennial groundwater recharge.
questions.explanation: The CWC, under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, does monitor live storage in major reservoirs and publishes regular bulletins — correct. The northeast (retreating) monsoon is indeed the principal rainy season for Tamil Nadu and the southern peninsula after the southwest monsoon withdraws — correct. Hydropower output depends directly on reservoir head and storage, not groundwater recharge, making statement 3 false.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Thirsty farms, slowing turbines: how depleting dams threaten power, harvest
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional mandate of the Central Water Commission and monsoon mechanics behind reservoir-linked hydropower, akin to UPSC's recurring questions on river basin/monsoon systems.

questions.stem: With reference to the CRPF's planned acquisition of 'FPV kamikaze drones', which one of the following best describes such a system?
options: An uncrewed aerial vehicle remotely piloted using a first-person video feed, designed to crash into its target carrying an explosive warhead and destroy itself on impact.
A fully autonomous aerial vehicle guided solely by GPS waypoints that loiters indefinitely over a target area until recalled by its operator.
A tethered aerial surveillance platform that streams continuous footage but cannot carry any payload.
A long-endurance, high-altitude unmanned aircraft used mainly for strategic reconnaissance, similar to a MALE/HALE drone.
questions.explanation: FPV (first-person-view) kamikaze drones are remotely flown by an operator viewing a live video feed, and they strike and self-destroy on impact with an explosive payload — matching the CRPF's draft specification. Option b describes a loitering munition's autonomy, not FPV's manual remote piloting. Option c is wrong since the whole point of a kamikaze drone is carrying a warhead. Option d describes a strategic MALE/HALE platform, a different drone category altogether.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: CRPF plans to acquire UAVs with capacity to strike and surveillance
questions.pyqLink: Tests classification of unmanned aerial systems (FPV/kamikaze vs loitering munition vs MALE/HALE), a growing area given India's drone doctrine developments.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Strait of Hormuz. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
Iran lies on the northern shore of the Strait of Hormuz, while Oman lies on its southern shore.
The Strait of Hormuz is widely regarded as the world's most important chokepoint for seaborne petroleum shipments.
The Strait of Malacca, rather than the Strait of Hormuz, separates the Arabian Peninsula from the Iranian mainland.
questions.explanation: The Strait of Hormuz does link the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, has Iran on its northern shore and Oman (Musandam) on its southern shore, and is indeed the world's busiest oil chokepoint — statements 1-3 are correct. Statement 4 is false and self-contradictory: it is the Strait of Hormuz itself, not the Strait of Malacca (which lies between Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore), that separates the Arabian Peninsula from Iran.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Iran war: IOC to buy crude, LPG carriers as Strait of Hormuz disruptions drive freight costs
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of global maritime chokepoints, a recurring geography theme (cf. UPSC questions on the Strait of Malacca and Bab-el-Mandeb).

questions.stem: With reference to India's crude oil imports from Russia, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The European Union has banned the import of petroleum products refined from Russian crude oil.
India is currently the largest importer of Russian crude oil, ahead of China.
questions.explanation: The EU has indeed banned imports of fuels refined from Russian crude, which is precisely why the Netherlands' difficulty in tracing oil origins matters for sanctions enforcement — statement 1 is correct. China, not India, remains the largest buyer of Russian crude; India is the second-largest, making statement 2 false.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Netherlands says 'difficult' to track product origin, remains among top buyers as India continues Russian oil purchase
questions.pyqLink: Tests awareness of EU sanctions architecture on Russian energy exports and India's position in global crude trade, relevant to GS-II/III international economic relations.

questions.stem: Statement-I: India's foreign exchange reserves declined in the week ended 30 October 2026, which does not necessarily indicate a deterioration in India's external financial position. Statement-II: Part of the decline reflects the RBI's deployment of funds mobilised through the FCNR(B) swap facility introduced to attract foreign currency deposits from Non-Resident Indians.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Reserves fell partly due to forex market intervention and valuation changes, but the deployment of dollars raised through the FCNR(B) swap facility is explicitly cited as a contributing factor, making Statement-II a correct and relevant explanation of Statement-I. FCNR(B) deposits are foreign-currency fixed deposits from NRIs that the RBI swapped into reserves earlier in 2026, so their subsequent deployment legitimately explains part of the drawdown without signalling external vulnerability.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's forex reserves fall $2.69 billion to $717 billion: Why RBI is selling dollars and what it means for the rupee
questions.pyqLink: Tests the FCNR(B) deposit scheme and how forex reserve movements are read in relation to external sector health, a recurring RBI/monetary economy theme.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of fertilizers and their primary plant nutrient. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Urea is the principal nitrogenous fertilizer, DAP the key phosphatic fertilizer, and MOP (potassium chloride) the main potassic/potash fertilizer — all three pairs are correctly matched. NPKS is a complex fertilizer supplying Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium and Sulphur together, not just nitrogen and phosphorus, making the fourth pair incorrect.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Fertilizer availability comfortable for rabi sowing, stock position exceeds requirement across key nutrients
questions.pyqLink: Tests basic fertilizer-nutrient classification underlying India's Nutrient Based Subsidy regime, relevant to agriculture economics in the Economy syllabus.

questions.stem: With reference to the Supreme Court's recent ruling on a State's power to levy a surcharge on sales tax, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Supreme Court held that a State surcharge computed on sales tax payable is a valid exercise of the State's power to tax the sale of goods and not an impermissible 'tax on tax'.
Statement-II: Article 271 of the Constitution confines the power to levy a surcharge on any tax or duty to the Union Parliament alone, and States have no corresponding power.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I reflects the Court's actual holding, grounded in the State's plenary power under Entry 54 of the State List (read with Article 246) to tax the sale of goods, which was held to encompass a surcharge as an additional sales tax rather than a tax on tax. Statement-II is also factually correct as a standalone constitutional provision — Article 271 lets Parliament surcharge duties/taxes referred to in Articles 269 and 270 for Union purposes — but it concerns the Union's own power over specific shared/assigned taxes, not the States' independent taxing power under List II, so it does not explain Statement-I.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Can states levy a tax on sales tax? The 30-year-old legal question SC has now settled, explained
questions.pyqLink: Tests distribution of legislative/taxation powers (Seventh Schedule, Article 246, Article 271) — similar in spirit to UPSC 2015/2018 questions on Constitutional provisions for Centre-State fiscal relations.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and their nodal Ministry/Department:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: PLI Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
PLI Scheme for Solar PV Modules
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
PLI Scheme for Food Processing Industries
questions.explanation: The Medical Devices PLI is run by the Department of Pharmaceuticals, the Electronics PLI by MeitY, and the Solar PV PLI by MNRE — all correctly matched. The Food Processing PLI (PLISFPI) is administered by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, not the Ministry of Textiles, making the fourth pair incorrect. Hence only three pairs are correctly matched.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Centre relaxes norms for medical device manufacturers amid 80% unused outlay
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional detail of PLI schemes and nodal ministries, a recurring UPSC theme (e.g., UPSC 2020 on schemes and implementing ministries).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB):
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The CPCB is a statutory body originally constituted under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
CPCB functions under the administrative control of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
The National Ambient Air Quality Standards prescribed by CPCB include limits for pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10 and ground-level ozone.
CPCB's continuous ambient air quality monitors can record particulate matter concentrations without any upper calibration limit.
questions.explanation: CPCB was constituted under the Water Act, 1974 and later entrusted powers under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981; it functions under the Union Environment Ministry; and NAAQS covers PM2.5, PM10, ozone and other pollutants — all correct. The fourth statement is false: as the CPCB itself clarified, its analysers measure only in the 0–1,000 µg/m³ range and log readings beyond this as 'outside range', i.e., they do have an upper calibration limit.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Amid concerns over data gaps, higher AQI on private platforms, CPCB clarifies
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory basis and functions of CPCB under the Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 — a recurring static institutional theme in Environment questions.

questions.stem: With reference to atmospheric science, which one of the following best describes 'photochemical smog'?
options: Haze formed when fine particulate matter and soot accumulate in cold, moisture-laden air near the ground, reducing visibility without any chemical transformation of pollutants
An atmospheric phenomenon caused by the direct emission of ground-level ozone from vehicular exhaust and industrial combustion sources
A type of smog formed exclusively through the condensation of water vapour around industrial soot particles in high-humidity, low-temperature conditions typical of winter mornings
A secondary form of air pollution produced when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react in the presence of sunlight to form ground-level ozone and other oxidants
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is a secondary pollution phenomenon: nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds undergo sunlight-driven reactions to generate ground-level ozone and other oxidants, which is why it is more common in sunny conditions. Ground-level ozone is never directly emitted, ruling out option B; options A and C describe particulate/condensation-based haze (closer to Delhi's winter smog), which is a physical accumulation process, not a photochemical one.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: What is smog and why does it blanket Delhi every winter?
questions.pyqLink: Tests atmospheric chemistry concept of primary vs secondary pollutants and photochemical reactions — related to UPSC's recurring questions on ground-level ozone and air pollutants.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Kumbh Mela tradition, in the context of Ujjain's preparations for Simhastha 2028:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Ujjain is one of the four traditional sites where the Kumbh Mela, locally known as Simhastha, is held on a rotational basis.
The timing of the Simhastha Mela at Ujjain is fixed purely by the solar Makar Sankranti transition and does not depend on the position of any planet.
Along with the melas at Haridwar, Prayagraj and Nashik, the Kumbh Mela tradition has been inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
The Simhastha Mela at Ujjain is held every six years, alternating with the Ardh Kumbh held at Haridwar.
questions.explanation: Ujjain (on the Shipra) is indeed one of the four Kumbh sites along with Haridwar, Prayagraj and Nashik, and the Kumbh Mela tradition was inscribed by UNESCO in 2017 — both correct. The timing of Simhastha is actually determined by Jupiter's entry into Leo (Simha rashi), not solely by Makar Sankranti, making the second statement false. The Ujjain Simhastha follows a twelve-year (duodecennial) cycle, as the article itself notes, not a six-year cycle — making the fourth statement false too. So only two statements are correct.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: A temple town in makeover mode: Ujjain gets another Rs 950-crore push ahead of Simhastha
questions.pyqLink: Tests static knowledge of the four Kumbh Mela sites, their astrological basis, and UNESCO intangible heritage inscription — similar to UPSC's culture/heritage-list questions.

questions.stem: With reference to the physical and administrative geography of the region where the Kolkata–Sairang Express derailed, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Northeast Frontier Railway zone, under whose jurisdiction the derailment occurred, has its headquarters at Maligaon in Guwahati, Assam.
The Brahmaputra river enters India from China through Arunachal Pradesh and flows through Assam before entering Bangladesh.
Kamrup (Metropolitan) district, where the derailment occurred, lies entirely on the southern bank of the Brahmaputra river.
questions.explanation: The Northeast Frontier Railway is headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati, and the Brahmaputra does enter India through Arunachal Pradesh before traversing Assam into Bangladesh — both correct. However, Kamrup (Metropolitan) district straddles both banks of the Brahmaputra, including North Guwahati on the northern bank, so it does not lie entirely on the southern bank, making the third statement incorrect.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Mizoram-bound Kolkata-Sairang Express train derails in Assam
questions.pyqLink: Tests river geography (Brahmaputra's course and entry point) and railway zone headquarters — a recurring static-geography pairing with current transport news.

questions.stem: With reference to the concept of collective defence invoked in the context of the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty embodies the principle of collective defence, under which an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all members.
India is a member of NATO's Partnership for Peace programme, which allows it limited participation in North Atlantic Council deliberations.
questions.explanation: Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty does codify collective defence — an attack on one ally is treated as an attack on all. India, however, is not a member of NATO or its Partnership for Peace programme; India has consistently maintained strategic autonomy and engages with such security architectures only through bilateral or issue-based arrangements, not alliance membership.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Third time's the charm? What US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks could yield, the role India can play
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of collective security/collective defence (NATO Article 5) and India's non-aligned posture — connects to UPSC's recurring international-organisations questions.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court recently held that commercial crop cultivation inside reserve forests is not protected under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, distinguishing such cultivators from the forest-dwelling communities the Act protects. In this context, consider the following statements. 1. The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 recognises forest rights only in favour of forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers who have been in occupation of forest land for generations, and not in favour of commercial plantation activity. 2. The Central Empowered Committee, which examines compliance with forest and wildlife laws, is a statutory body constituted under the Indian Forest Act, 1927. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 recognises forest rights only in favour of forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers who have been in occupation of forest land for generations, and not in favour of commercial plantation activity.
The Central Empowered Committee, which examines compliance with forest and wildlife laws, is a statutory body constituted under the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct and is exactly the distinction the Supreme Court drew in this case: FRA protects generational forest-dwelling ST/OTFD communities, not sponsored commercial cultivation. Statement 2 is wrong because the Central Empowered Committee was constituted by Supreme Court orders and derives statutory backing from a notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, not the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Commercial cultivation within forest land not protected under FRA, 2006: Supreme Court
questions.pyqLink: Tests the scope of rights under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and the statutory basis of the Central Empowered Committee; similar to UPSC prelims questions on FRA rights-holders.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court's order concerned silk cotton cultivation inside the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve. Consider the following statements regarding Biosphere Reserves in India. 1. Biosphere Reserves in India are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. 2. A Biosphere Reserve is typically organised into a core zone, a buffer zone and a transition zone. 3. The Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, spanning parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, is included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves. 4. Every Biosphere Reserve in India is also declared a Ramsar site. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: Biosphere Reserves in India are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
A Biosphere Reserve is typically organised into a core zone, a buffer zone and a transition zone.
The Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, spanning parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, is included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
Every Biosphere Reserve in India is also declared a Ramsar site.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the core-buffer-transition zonation is the standard Biosphere Reserve design, and Agasthyamalai is a UNESCO-recognised Biosphere Reserve straddling Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Statement 1 is wrong because Biosphere Reserve designation is an administrative/international (UNESCO MAB) recognition, not a notification under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Statement 4 is wrong since Ramsar status applies specifically to wetlands and is a separate designation, not automatic for Biosphere Reserves.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Commercial cultivation within forest land not protected under FRA, 2006: Supreme Court
questions.pyqLink: Tests the UNESCO Man and Biosphere Programme zonation and designation process, a recurring static theme in prelims questions on Biosphere Reserves.

questions.stem: In the context of the reported data gaps in Delhi's air quality monitoring during Deepavali, consider the following pairs.
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Particulate matter of diameter 2.5 micrometres or less, fine enough to penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream
Particulate matter of diameter 10 micrometres or less, which chiefly affects the upper respiratory tract
A statutory body established under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Published daily by the Ministry of Earth Sciences using data from its weather monitoring network

The AQI pair is wrong because the National Air Quality Index is compiled and published by the CPCB under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which instead runs the separate SAFAR forecasting system through IITM.

questions.sourceTitle: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi

questions.stem: News reports note that an exceptionally strong El Nino is intensifying global warming and disrupting weather patterns in 2026. In this context, consider the following statements. 1. El Nino events are always accompanied by below-normal Indian summer monsoon rainfall. 2. El Nino refers to the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. 3. El Nino conditions are typically associated with a weakening of trade winds and suppressed upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water off the Peruvian coast. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: El Nino events are always accompanied by below-normal Indian summer monsoon rainfall.
El Nino refers to the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean.
El Nino conditions are typically associated with a weakening of trade winds and suppressed upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water off the Peruvian coast.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correctly describe El Nino as a warming of Pacific sea surface temperatures linked to weakened trade winds and suppressed Peruvian upwelling. Statement 1 overstates the link: El Nino is only correlated, not invariably linked, with a weak Indian monsoon, and several El Nino years have recorded near-normal rainfall, which is why the word 'always' makes it incorrect.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: El Nino Watch: the impacts around the world this week
questions.pyqLink: Tests the ocean-atmosphere mechanics of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation and its monsoon linkage, a recurring prelims theme.

questions.stem: Reports on the global stock sell-off noted that Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities even as Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) were net sellers. In this context, consider the following statements. 1. Foreign Portfolio Investors pool funds raised domestically within India and invest them in markets abroad. 2. Domestic Institutional Investors are foreign entities registered with SEBI that invest in Indian markets using funds pooled overseas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Foreign Portfolio Investors pool funds raised domestically within India and invest them in markets abroad.
Domestic Institutional Investors are foreign entities registered with SEBI that invest in Indian markets using funds pooled overseas.
questions.explanation: Both statements are incorrect because they swap the two categories. FPIs are foreign entities registered with SEBI under the SEBI (FPI) Regulations that bring funds pooled abroad into Indian markets, the reverse of statement 1. DIIs, such as domestic mutual funds, insurance companies and banks, invest using funds mobilised within India, not funds registered as foreign or pooled overseas as statement 2 claims.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
questions.pyqLink: Tests precise definitions of FPI and DII in Indian capital markets, similar to prelims questions on SEBI's FPI Regulations.

questions.stem: The Global Carbon Project's 2026 assessment noted that global carbon dioxide emissions dipped slightly due to oil-supply disruption rather than a shift to clean energy. With reference to global climate science, which one of the following best describes the term 'global carbon budget'?
options: It is the maximum cumulative amount of carbon dioxide that can still be emitted globally while keeping warming within a given temperature target, tracked against actual emissions from fossil fuels, land-use change and natural sinks.
It is the annual financial allocation made under the UNFCCC to fund climate adaptation projects in developing countries.
It is the mandatory national emission-reduction target every country must meet each year under its Nationally Determined Contribution.
It is the total renewable energy capacity that G20 countries agreed to install by 2030.
questions.explanation: The global carbon budget is the remaining cumulative quantity of CO2 emissions consistent with a chosen warming limit, which is precisely what the Global Carbon Project tracks annually against fossil-fuel, land-use and natural-sink flows. The other options wrongly describe climate finance mechanisms (Adaptation Fund/Green Climate Fund), NDC emission targets, and the renewables-tripling pledge, none of which is what 'carbon budget' means.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Heat-trapping carbon pollution drops, but scientists cite Iran war rather than energy progress
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static climate-science concept of the 'carbon budget' used in IPCC assessments, distinct from climate-finance and NDC terminology.
